title: Leafminer on Watermelon-Kenya
text: Leafminer on Watermelon-Kenya

title: Leafminer on Watermelon-Kenya
text: * Rotate melon with other non-host crops such as maize, legumes, carrots and onions. * Mulch the plants to prevent larvae from getting to the soil to pupate. * Avoid planting new crop next to a previously affected crop. * Plough deep after harvesting crop. * Fertilise adequately to ensure plant health with both organic and inorganic fertilisers. * Remove weeds as they serve as a reservoir for leafminers.

title: Leafminer on Watermelon-Kenya
text:
* Additional relevant crops: tomatoes, courgettes, bean, eggplant, pepper, potato, squash. * Look out for:
* Stippled appearance on foliage caused by egg laying female insects. * Slender white winding leaf mines (whitish blotches) on the surface of the leaves. * Colourless to yellowish green larvae with black mouth. * Trap adult flies by placing 3 x 5 inch yellow sticky farms in the farm. * Take action when 5% crop is affected.

title: Leafminer on Watermelon-Kenya
text: * Placing of yellow stick traps in the farm to reduce population of adults. * Use of Natural enemies­parasitic wasps like *Chrysocharis oscinidis* and *Diglyphus isaea*. * Soil drenching with *metarhizium* 69 to kill pupae in the soil at the rate of 80mls per acre. * Physically crushing the larvae once first sign of tunneling is observed. * Spraying neem oil at rates of 40mls at 20l of water. * Destroy infested plants to ensure field hygiene by burning or burying.

title: Leafminer on Watermelon-Kenya
text: * When using a pesticide always wear protective gear. * Follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval. * Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).

title: Leafminer on Watermelon-Kenya
text:
### Spray bifenthrin e.g. Brigade EC at a rate of 20 ml in 20 litres of water. Non-systemic with contact stomach action. Pyrethroid; IRAC 3A. ###
WHO class II (Moderately hazardous). PHI 3 days. MRL 1.0 mg/Kg
### Drench with imidacloprid e.g. Confidor 010 UL at a rate of 10ml in 20 litres of water. Neonicitinoid; IRAC 4A. Systemic insecticide with translaminar activity and with contact and stomach action. ###
WHO Class II. MRL 0.5 mg/Kg. Spray early morning or late evening to avoid harming bees.

title: Root knot nematode in tomato-Kenya
text: Root knot nematode in tomato-Kenya

title: Root knot nematode in tomato-Kenya
text: * Collect soil and water samples for analysis at KALRO Kabete or any other certified laboratory to determine presence of root-knot nematodes. * Rotate tomato with maize, wheat, finger millet, kale or cabbage for 3 cropping seasons to control nematodes. * Plant clean certified seedlings from a certified nursery. * Use clean irrigation water that is free from nematodes. * Solarize soil by covering with plastic sheet for 8-12 weeks depending on intensity of the sun's heat. * Plant antagonistic plants such as marigold in the field to control nematodes. * Maintain good soil health and high level of organic matter, e.g. applying manure. * Wash off soil on all farm tools and disinfect with chlorine-based, approved products.

title: Root knot nematode in tomato-Kenya
text: * Look for stunted growth, yellowing on leaves and wilting of plants even when soil has adequate moisture. Affected plants appear in patches. * Look for swollen lumps or galls on the roots that do not detach easily by touching. * Before planting, take action when soil test results show 1-10 root- knot nematodes in 200g of soil. * After planting take action if 1 out of 5 plants are infected in the field.

title: Root knot nematode in tomato-Kenya
text: * Uproot infected plants and debris and destroy by burning. * Drench the root zone at transplanting with Azadirachtin based products. Repeat this after 2 weeks. * Use *Purpureocillium lilacinum* based products. * Use *Trichoderma asperellum* based products.

title: Root knot nematode in tomato-Kenya
text:
* Always use products registered by PCPB for target crops and pests: www.pcpb.go.ke
* Before use, read and follow pesticide product label instructions e.g. PHI, REI, usage and disposal of pesticide waste. * Always wear appropriate protective equipment.

title: Root knot nematode in tomato-Kenya
text:
### Spray around the root zone with Fosthiazate based products. ###
Not classified by WHO. ### Apply Dazomet based products as pre-plant soil fumigant ###
WHO Class III (Slightly hazardous). ### For greenhouse production disinfect the soil with metam-sodium based products. ###
WHO Class II (Moderately hazardous). ### Apply Carvacrol based products as a drench ###
Not classified by WHO.

title: Chocolate spot on faba bean-Ethiopia
text: Chocolate spot on faba bean-Ethiopia

title: Chocolate spot on faba bean-Ethiopia
text: * Use improved varieties Alloshe, Numan, Ashebeka, Tumsa, Dosha, Obse, Gebelcho or Moti. Plant seeds free from chocolate spot disease. * Practice crop rotation every 2-3 years with non-host crops (Wheat, Barley, Maize). * Do not sow disease free seeds in previously chocolate spot pathogen infected field, use disease free seeds in disease free field or keep a distance of at least 500m from infected fields. * Avoid high planting density this will reduce the humidity which triggers the aggressive phase of the disease. Check correct spacing for each variety. * Remove crop debris and volunteer bean plants like chickpea, lentils, vetch beans etc) and destroy by burning. * Make sure adequate drainage is provided and use correct rate of fertilizer. * Minimize movement from infected to disease free fields. * Deep plowing of the fields with high chocolate spot infection immediately after harvest reduces the risk of disease development. * Seed treatment of *Rhizobium* (10 g/kg faba bean seeds) before sowing improve plant health and indirectily reduce chocolate spot severity.

title: Chocolate spot on faba bean-Ethiopia
text: * Start monitoring the crop from emergence of leaves until maturity as there are 2 phases to the disease. * There are 2 disease phases. Non-aggressive phase: look for small brown/red spots peppered over the leaves also on stems, pods and flowers. * During high humidity the aggressive phase develops: grey fungus grows on the spots as they become larger and darker, defoliation can follow. Young pods and flower can abort or become stunted. Brown streaks appear on stems and can cause them to lodge. * Consider applying a protectant fungicide when plants show the first symptoms of the disease espcially if the weather is forcasted to be wet - taking action when there are 5-10 spots per leaf or 3-5 leaves per plant infected. * Sowing date with a resistant (tolerant) variety and judicious use of fungicide can be used as good option of chocolate spot management.

title: Chocolate spot on faba bean-Ethiopia
text: * Remove severely affected plants and destroy by burying or burning to reduce the source of inoculum on the farm

title: Chocolate spot on faba bean-Ethiopia
text: * When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label. * Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance. * Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of MoA, Plant Health Regulatory Directorate, Ethiopia.

title: Chocolate spot on faba bean-Ethiopia
text:
### Mancozeb (Sancozeb 80% WP). Concider applying as a protectant before infestation at a rate of 0.7 kg/Ha. A protectant fungicide with multi-site contact activity, FRAC group: M3 ###
WHO U (Unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use). 3-4 applications during a season with a 7-14 day interval between applications. Mancozeb is very toxic to fish and other aquatic organisms. ### Apply Mancozeb 64% w/w + Metalaxyl-M 4% (Ridomil Gold SL) at a rate of 2.5kg/ha using 200-250 L of water. A protectant contact/systemic fungicide. Mancozeb FRAC group M3 and Metalaxyl-M FRAC group 4 ###
WHO III. 1-2 applications per season within 7-10 days interval. Ridomil Gold SL is very toxic to fish and other aquatic organisms. Don't wash it in water bodies. REI 48hrs. ### Apply Chlorothalonil (Rova 75 WP) at a rate of 2.5kg/ha. Multi-site contact activity, FRAC group M5 ###
WHO U (Unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use) Apply at weekly intervals.

title: Late blight of potato-Ethiopia
text: Late blight of potato-Ethiopia

title: Late blight of potato-Ethiopia
text:
* Use disease free planting material. Inspect seed potatoes to make sure there is no disease before planting
* Use quality declared seed (QDS). IDM improved potato varieties: Gudene, Belete, Jalene, Zenegena, Chiro, Bubu, Gorobella
* Crop rotation - avoid planting tomato, pepper and other solanaceous crops if late blight is present. * Remove left overs plants that can serve as source of the inoculum
* Plant early. For ware potatoes adopt 0.75m X 0.30m between rows and plants and 0.30m X 0.60m for seed use. Use the recommended fertilizer rate since the pathogen develops fast under high nitrogen conditions
* Do not over water and maintain good drainage
* Hill or earth up the soil over the planted seed potatoes can protect the tubers from the disease
* Dehulm and remove the vines 15 days before harvest. Do not compost cull piles, chop and bury
* During harvest remove damaged and diseased tubers. Avoid wounding tubers and remove soil before transport
* Remove infected seed tubers from the store and bury

title: Late blight of potato-Ethiopia
text:
* Inspect the field for disease every other day after plant emergence
* Leaf lesions are highly variable depending on environmental condition and cultivar
* Initial symptoms: small, pale or dark green spots with yellow halos. Growing rapidly into large brown to purple/black lesions that eventually kill the plant. Under moist conditions, white cottony structures appears at the edge of the lesion mostly on the underside of the leaves
* Infected stem have irregular lesions surrowned by white cottony structure and are brittle
* Symptom on infected tubers: irregular, slightly depressed areas brown to purple in colour. On the skin they can show as redish brown superficial or deep rotted areas accompanied by secondory infection
* Scout suspect low-lying areas which tend to dry out more slowly, the disease might be more likely to occur here
* When symptoms are at around 5% serverity carry out control methods

title: Late blight of potato-Ethiopia
text:
* Remove the diseased plants and plant parts by bagging them to avoid producing large numbers of spores that could put other plants and nearby farmers at risk
* Destroy diseased plant parts outside the field by burying 1m under the ground
* Kill vines totally prior to harvest because late blight does not sporulate on dead plant tissue. It's an obligate parasite
* Infected tubers should not be stored. Monitor storage carefully for any sign of tuber decay

title: Late blight of potato-Ethiopia
text: * When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label. Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance. All products toxic to fish and aquatic organisms, do not spray near water. Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of MoA, Plant Health Regulatory Directorate, Ethiopia

title: Late blight of potato-Ethiopia
text:
### Mancozeb (Ridom 80% WP, Sabozeb 80% WP, Ethiozeb 80% WP) Apply at a rate of 1.5-2.5 kg/ha. FRAC group M3 ###
WHO class U. Apply every 7-10 days, check lable for maximum applications. PHI 14 days. ### Metalaxyl-M 4% w/w + Mancozeb 64% w/w (Ridomil Gold) Applied at 2.5 Kg/ha. Metalaxyl-M FRAC 4; Mancozeb FRAC M3 ###
Mancozeb WHO class U + Metalaxyl-M WHO class II. Apply every 10-14 days. Do not apply more than 3 times in a season. PHI 7 days. ### Famoxadone 22.5% + Cymoxanil 30% (Equation Pro WDG; Gachena 525 WG). Apply at a rate of 400g/ha/200-300 L of water. Famoxadone FRAC 11 + Cymoxanil FRAC 27 ###
Famoxadone (WHO class U) + Cymoxanil (WHO class II) Apply every 7-14 days. PHI 14 days. ### Copper hydroxide (Champion, Kocide 101) Apply at a rate of 2-3 kg/ha. FRAC M1 ###
WHO class II (Moderately hazardous). Apply every 7-10 days, check label for maximum applications. PHI 0 days, REI 24hrs.

title: Powdery mildew on mango-Ethiopia
text: Powdery mildew on mango-Ethiopia

title: Powdery mildew on mango-Ethiopia
text:
* Use resistant varieties and ensure transplanting of seedlings free from powdery mildew disease
* Plant at proper spacing usually 6m x 6m (but this will depend on the variety)
* Carry out regular pruning of tree branches, this allow good air circulation reduces humidity in the canpoy that favors the establishment, development and reproduction of the pathogen
* Pick up fallen leaves and flowers and bury 60cm deep as these can harbour the fungus and help spread the disease
* Use clean pruning equipment to avoid contamination, use fire to sterilise
* In nurseries, avoid overhead watering to reduce the relative humidity as excessive watering increases the incidence of the disease
* Minimize movement from infected to disease free fields

title: Powdery mildew on mango-Ethiopia
text:
* Before blossoming, mark 5 trees/ha randomly in orchard and check for symptoms of the disease each week:
* Young infected leaves develop grey necrotic lesions on the upper side of leaves and tend to curl downwards - If severe, the leaves may become brown, dry and fall
* Flowers fail to open, blacken or become brown and dry and may fall from panicles as they become completely covered by the fungus - A severe blossom infection can result in complete loss of fruit
* If young fruit is infected the skin cracks becomes corky, this may cover the entire fruit
* Carry out control measures when 5% symptoms severity is observed

title: Powdery mildew on mango-Ethiopia
text:
* Carry out phytosanitary pruning by removing all infected twigs, branches and panicles. Destroy these by burning or bury 60cm deep. Do not compost infected plant debris
* Spray infected shoots with a solution of 6 spoons of baking powder, 3 spoons of white oil and white bar soap foam and Mix in 15 litres of water and spray every week to reduce infection

title: Powdery mildew on mango-Ethiopia
text: * There are no registered fungicides in Ethiopia for the management of powdery mildew on mango.

title: Paddy mites-India
text: Paddy mites-India

title: Paddy mites-India
text: * Sowing is suggested during early April. * Maintain black gram (variety ADT 5), and cowpea as border crops to encourage multiplication of natural enemies like predatory mites, coccinellid beetles, anthocorid bugs, and staphylinid beetles. * Avoid excess amount of Nitrogen application. * Apply urea in three equal splits and use LCC for application of nitrogenous fertilizers.

title: Paddy mites-India
text: * Observe for the occurrence of eggs, nymphs and adults on the lower surface of the leaves using a hand lens during hot summer and humid climate (May – June). * Observe for the development of intermittent red and yellow patches on the leaves and whitening of leaves. * Monitor the symptoms during prolonged dry spell periods.

title: Paddy mites-India
text: * Flood the nursery with water for about 15 minutes and then drain. * Application of 3% Neem oil @ 100ml/ 8 cents of nursery.

title: Paddy mites-India
text: * Use of personal protective equipment (PPEs) such as hand gloves, mask, goggles and keeping antidotes are mandatory by the spray applicators.

title: Paddy mites-India
text:
### Spray Propargite 57% EC: 250 ml per acre (Spray Wettable sulphur @ 3 g / litre, e.g. Thiovit, Sulfex) ###
WHO class III (moderately hazardous). ### Spray Fenpyroximate 5% SC: 60 ml per ###
WHO class II (moderately hazardous). ### Spray Spiromesifen 22.9% SC:@ 250 ml per ###
Not classified by WHO
### Spray Profenofos @2.0 ml / litre (e.g. Curacron, Carina, Profex) ###
WHO class II (moderately hazardous).

title: Fall armyworm on maize
text: UK, CABI: Fall armyworm on maize

title: Fall armyworm on maize
text:
* Avoid late planting or off-season planting and avoid planting new crop near infested fields
* Use a mixture of maize varieties when planting; varieties showing resistance/tolerance, short duration or increased leaf toughness. * Avoid staggered plantings (plots of different ages)
* Ensure optimum use of fertilizer for strong maize plants able to compensate for damage done and apply at the right time
* Keep the surroundings of the plot free of grass weeds
* Conserve shelters and flowering plants on the edges for beneficial insects such as ground beetles and parasitoids
* Intercrop maize with crops not susceptible to FAW such as cassava or yam, or with less susceptible crops such as cowpeas or beans
* Avoid spraying insecticides early in the crop cycle as this will kill natural enemies that control the pest, and it might not be economical
* Do not move infested plant material from the farm to reduce spread

title: Fall armyworm on maize
text:
* Start monitoring as soon as the plant emerges
* Monitor 10 consecutive plants in 10 locations of the field
* Look for creamy/grey egg masses covered in silk located on the underside or top of the leaves and on the stems
* Look for light green/dark brown caterpillars with longitudinal stripes, dark head with an upside down pate Y-shaped. The second-to-last body segment has 4 dark spots forming a square. Do so in early morning or evening hours
* Look for light coloured patches (“window panes”) to large ragged and elongated holes in the leaves emerging from the whorl
* Look for caterpillars and accumulation of frass in the whorl or burrowed into the side of the cobs
* At early whorl stage, take action if >20% of plants are damaged or infested with larvae. At late whorl stage, if small larvae can be found then take action if >40% of whorls are damaged. At tassel and silk stage, do not spray anymore

title: Fall armyworm on maize
text:
* On small-scale farms, handpick and destroy the egg masses and larvae
* If available, spray young caterpillars with neem-based products before they enter the ears or whorl

title: Stem rust (black rust) on wheat-Ethiopia
text: Stem rust (black rust) on wheat-Ethiopia

title: Stem rust (black rust) on wheat-Ethiopia
text:
* Use certified, disease-free seed
* Plant resistant varieties: Mendoyu, Gelan, Sinja and Sanate
* When selecting varieties make sure they are suitable for the altitude where they will be grown
* Avoid planting new wheat crop next to an infected field
* Avoid walking through fields during the wet season to prevent disease spread from one plant to another
* Rotate wheat with non-cereal crops: beans and other vegetables
* Remove volunteer plants and alternative hosts (barberry and barley) before planting
* Follow disease forecasting systems from national and international information centers
* Prevent movement of infected plants across the field
* Start working from the healthy part of the field before moving to the infected part

title: Stem rust (black rust) on wheat-Ethiopia
text:
* Additional relevant crops: barley
* Start field observation 3-4 weeks after planting especially if the weather is warm and the humidity high
* Inspect for orange pustules surrounded by a halo at the margin
* Look for elongated reddish-brown pustules on stems and both sides of leaves
* Pustules dislodge orange to blackish spores
* Take action once a single pustule is observed

title: Stem rust (black rust) on wheat-Ethiopia
text: * Remove and bury infected plant materials below 50 cm in the ground

title: Stem rust (black rust) on wheat-Ethiopia
text:
* When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
* Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
* Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of MoA, Plant Health Regulatory Directorate, Ethiopia

title: Stem rust (black rust) on wheat-Ethiopia
text:
### Propiconazole (Tilt 250EC, Albu, Bumper 25 EC, Panazole 25% EC) Apply at a rate of 0.5 L/ha. A systemic curative and prrotectant triazole fungicide, FRAC group: 3 ###
WHO II (Moderately hazardous). Toxic to aquatic organisms do not use near waterways. No more than 2 applications per season. PHI 45 days
### Triadimefon (Bayleton 25 WP, Noble 25 WP) Apply at a rate of 2.5-3.75 kg/ha. A systemic curative and prrotectant triazole fungicide, FRAC group: 3 ###
WHO II (Moderately hazardous). Apply at first signs of the disease and again if infection occurs again. PHI 28 days, REI 6 hours. Toxic to aquatic organisms do not use near waterways
### Tebuconazole (Bless). Systemic fungicide used as foliar spray. Spray at a rate of 0.5l/ha by dissolving in 200-250 l of water ###
WHO II (Moderately hasardous). Moderately toxic to water organisms, birds and pollinators. PHI-30 days and REI-12 hours

title: Maize Lethal Necrosis Disease (MLND) -Ethiopia
text: Maize Lethal Necrosis Disease (MLND) -Ethiopia

title: Maize Lethal Necrosis Disease (MLND) -Ethiopia
text:
* Use MLND free certified seed from registered suppliers (enterprises, cooperatives, agrodealers) – This disease is seed borne as well as transmitted by vectors
* Do not move infected maize plants and seeds to MLND free areas and avoid planting maize if an infected field is less than 500m away
* Rotate with none cereal crops (beans, faba bean, chickpea, onion and vegetables) for at least 2-3 years/seasons
* Remove alternate hosts (sorghum, grasses, millet, wheat, oats, sudan grass) and contol insect vectors (see yellow column)
* Burn maize residues in the field after harvest
* Leave land fallow for 2 months especially where maize is produced both in main season using rain and off-season using irrigation. Plough and expose soil to sun light for at least 2 months before planting
* Eliminate alternative host plants (weeds) of thrips, aphids and plant hoppers and clear/burn grasses around the field that could serve as a potential reservior of the insect vectors
* Synchronize planting date among farmers of the area to break continuous disease spread between fields
* Avoid physically transmission of MLND since the virus can be carried on clothes
* The use of MLN disease resistant variety/ies in the future which are under development

title: Maize Lethal Necrosis Disease (MLND) -Ethiopia
text:
* Monitoring for MLNV should be carried out at a village level twice every week from crop emergence onwards
* Look for the insect vectors under the leaves in the morning thrips, aphids, beetles and plant hoppers. These insects are virus vectors and can transmit the disease
* Monitor the plant at all stages of plant growth since the MLN disease symptom/s could emerged at any of stage plant growth
* Intially monitor small yellow areas (mottling) on leaves, later the leaves become paler, and then the edges turn brown and dry inwards
* In some cases look for the dead heart and dead plant symptoms starting in the whorl of the plant. Shrivelled ears, little or no grain produced, dwarfing and premature aging of plants could be monitored at each respective plant growth stage
* The disease can be confused with maize streak virus which has thinner yellow stripes that do not merge and there is no marginal browning and drying up
* Rogue out when the infected plant population is low or below 5% of the total field
* Act immediately when symptoms are observed on a single plant – carry out direct controls (both green and yellow)

title: Maize Lethal Necrosis Disease (MLND) -Ethiopia
text:
* Rogue out all infected plants when observed in the field
* Carefully remove diseased maize from the field and either bury the plant residues into more than 1m soil deep, burn or feed to animals, if there is no development of secondary fungal infection (rotting) on grain or cobs
* Do not leave any diseased plants in the field as they will be a source of new infections

title: Maize Lethal Necrosis Disease (MLND) -Ethiopia
text:
* When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label. Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
* Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of MoA, Plant Health Regulatory Directorate, Ethiopia
* There are no chemical pesticides which can be used against MLND as it is a combination of viruses
* Insecticides can be used to manage the virus transmitting insect vectors but this should only be done if all diseased plants have been removed from the field

title: Maize Lethal Necrosis Disease (MLND) -Ethiopia
text:
### Imidacloprid (Tata mida 200SL) 6-10ml/20L; Systemic neconicoteinoid; IRAC mode of action: 4A ###
WHO class II (moderately hazardous), REI-12hrs, PHI 7-14 days, toxic to bees do not apply at tasselling
### Lambda-cyholothrin (Duduthrin 1.7 EC) 65ml/20L water; Contact and stomach action pyrethroid; IRAC mode of action: 3A ###
WHO class II (moderately hazardous), REI-24hrs, PHI 30 days, Apply twice in planting season, highly toxic to fish avoid spraying near water

title: Bacterial wilt disease in ginger-Ethiopia
text: Bacterial wilt disease in ginger-Ethiopia

title: Bacterial wilt disease in ginger-Ethiopia
text:
* Use disease free planting soil or fields that are free from the disease
* Use disease free planting rhizomes from the known sources or rhizome/seeding from tissue culture
* Use the appropriate or recommended planting space both between plants and planting rows to avoid transmission through contact. Planting in raised beds or ridges
* Rotate ginger with crops that are not hosts of the disease, such as maize, taro, sorghum
* Do not intercrop or rotate ginger with solanaceous crops such as potato, tomato, pepper, tobacco, eggplant
* Harvest on time to minimize crop exposure to the disease if the field is already infected
* Disinfect all farm tools by dipping in a disinfectant (household bleach diluted 1 part with 4 parts water)
* Ensure farmers start working from disease-free areas before moving to affected ones to prevent spread

title: Bacterial wilt disease in ginger-Ethiopia
text:
* Monitor for water-soaked spots/lesions on both pseudo-stem and leaves after emergence of the ginger plant
* Daily monitoring/observation for wilted yellow leaves which progress from the bottom upward, affecting the younger leaves and rapidly turning to yellow-brown
* Observe rapid yellowing due to ginger bacterial wilt pathogen within 3-5 days of water-soaked symptom emergence. * Monitor for rotting and a bad smell at the collar region or at the junction of the pseudo-stem and rhizomes
* Observe white, milky bacteria streaming by cutting and suspend the pseudo-stem or rhizome in clean beaker filled with clean water. * Immediate harvesting and drying for consumptions if the rhizome sets yields

title: Bacterial wilt disease in ginger-Ethiopia
text: * As soon as symptoms are seen, uproot infected plants and burn them

title: Bacterial wilt disease in ginger-Ethiopia
text: * There are no chemical pesticides currently registered in Ethiopia for management of this disease

title: Cotton bollworm on tomato-Kenya
text: CABI: Cotton bollworm on tomato-Kenya

title: Cotton bollworm on tomato-Kenya
text: * Avoid rotation with other host crops e.g. maize, beans, pepper, eggplants, wheat, barley or sorghum. * Plant a trap crop (e.g. African marigold) every 8 rows. * Plant tomatoes away from cotton or maize crops. * Remove any fallen fruit/infested plant parts and feed to livestock. * Conserve natural enemies by planting flower hedgerows and through minimizing use of broad spectrum insecticides. * Plough the field after harvesting to expose pupae to sunlight and natural enemies, and to incorporate crop residues.

title: Cotton bollworm on tomato-Kenya
text: * Inspect the crop 1-2 times/week throughout the season; randomly select 30 tomato plants for monitoring. * Look out for greenish to brown-black larvae on leaves, flowers & young fruits. * Look out for bored holes near the fruit stalk. * Take action when eggs & larvae are observed on most of the 30 plants.

title: Cotton bollworm on tomato-Kenya
text: * Release natural enemies e.g. egg parasitoids (*Trichogramma* spp. ), or larval parasitoids (*Cotesia* spp., *Bracon* spp.) * Apply Azadirachtin based products (neem). * Spray entomopathogenic fungi (*Metarhizium anisopliae* & *Beauveria bassiana*). * Apply product based on *Bacillus thuringiensis* var. kurstaki strain (against young larvae).

title: Cotton bollworm on tomato-Kenya
text: * PHI & MRL: Not applicable for biopesticides in WHO Class U. * When using a pesticide, always wear personnal protective equipment. * Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB). * Follow instructions on product label on PHI, dosage, usage & disposal. * Farmers to always seek technical advice. Pesticides need to target young larvae, before they enter the fruits. To reduce risk for resistance build-up, alternate pesticides from different classes, with different modes of action.

title: Cotton bollworm on tomato-Kenya
text:
### Apply Spinosad based products. ###
WHO class III (slightly hazardous). PHI 3 days. Toxic to bees, thus apply at night if crop is flowering. ### Apply Lambda-cyhalothrin based products. ###
WHO II (moderately hazardous). PHI 3 days, REI: 12 hours. Toxic to bees, thus apply at night if crop is flowering. ### Apply Chlorantraniliprole based products ###
WHO Class U (unlikely to present an acute hazard in normal use). PHI 1 day, REI 12h. Low toxicity to bees
### Apply Tebufenozide based products ###
WHO Class U (unlikely to present an acute hazard in normal use). PHI 7 days, REI 12h. Low toxicity to bees
### Apply Etofenprox based products ###
WHO Class U (unlikely to present an acute hazard in normal use). REI, when dried, PHI 7 days. Highly toxic to bees
### Apply Diafenthiuron based products ###
WHO II (moderately hazardous). PHI 3 days. Moderately toxic to bees

title: Whiteflies on tomato-Kenya
text: CABI: Whiteflies on tomato-Kenya

title: Whiteflies on tomato-Kenya
text: * Plant pest-free seedlings from certified sources. * Use clean, pest-free organic mulch after transplanting. * Destroy all host crops (*Tagetes*, amaranthus, old potato crop etc) and debris before planting. * Use a shade net (size 400 µm) / tunnel for 3-5 weeks while in nursery to prevent attack by white flies. * Conserve natural enemies (lace wing larvae, bugs) by leaving a natural hedge of flowering plants. * Plant repellent crops such as coriander or Mexican marigold after 3-4 rows of tomato to repel the white flies. * Plant trap crops like beans, maize among others around the field. * Avoid high doses of nitrogen fertiliser, which can make the plants more attractive to sucking pests

title: Whiteflies on tomato-Kenya
text: * Monitor with yellow sticky traps (at least one or two per acre) to check for general presence of the pest. * Look for whitish adults on the underside of young leaves. * Look for small white insects that fly when the plant is shaken. * Consider direct control when 3 adult white flies are present per leaf.

title: Whiteflies on tomato-Kenya
text: * Spray Azadirachtin based products (Neem). * Release natural enemies like *Encarsia* wasp (parasitoid wasp). * Spray *Beauveria bassiana*, and *Lecanicillium lecanii* at recommended rates. * Spray *Metarhizium anisopliae* based products.

title: Whiteflies on tomato-Kenya
text:
* General Pesticide Restrictions
* When using a pesticide always wear appropriate personal protective equipment. * Follow the instructions on the product label on dosage, maximum applications, PHI,Re-entry interval, disposal of pesticide waste amongst others. * Use list of registered pesticides (PCPB): www.pcpb.go.ke

text:

WHO Class II (Moderately hazardous)

WHO Class II (Moderately hazardous)

WHO Class II (Moderately hazardous)

WHO Class II (Moderately hazardous)

title: Kidungata cha muhogo
text: CABI: Kidungata cha muhogo

title: Kidungata cha muhogo
text: * Usitumie sehemu za mimea zilizoathirika. Kabla ya kupanda, vipande vya shina za mihogo, unaweza kuzitia kwenye maji moto (changanya viwango vinavyolingana vya moto na baridi) kwa muda wa dakika tano hadi kumi ili kuua vindungata. * Kama kuna uwezekano, panda aina ya mihogo yenye uwezo mdogo wa kushambuliwa na vidungata. * Panda mihogo mapema katika msimu wa mvua, ili iweze kukua vizuri kabla ya msimu wa kiangazi. Hii ni kwasababu mimea iliyo na nguvu, inaweza kustahimili mashambulio ya vidungata. * Tumia mbinu za marekebisho ya mchanga na uwekaji wa matandazo ili kuzuia kupotea kwa unyevunyevu hasa katika aina ya udongo ambao ni mbovu. Idadi ya vidungata huwa nyingi kwenye mihogo iliyopandwa kwenye udongo mbovu, na vinaweza kusababisha uharibifu hata kama maadui wao wa kawaida wako karibu. * Zuia usafirishaji wa sehemu za mimea zilizoathirika, katika mipaka au maeneo yasiyo na vidungata.

title: Kidungata cha muhogo
text: * Zuia usafirishaji wa sehemu za mimea zilizoathirika, katika mipaka au maeneo yasiyo na vidungata. * Kama inawezekana usipande mihogo katika shamba moja kwa zaidi ya miaka mitatu mfululizo.Fanya mapandikizi na mahindi au mimea kutoka kwa jamii ya mikunde.

title: Kidungata cha muhogo
text: * Angalia mimea yako kila wiki ili kuona kama imeshambuliwa na vidungata kwenye miche, mashina na matawi. * Vidungata vilivyopevuka vya kike na mabuu,vinaweza kuonekana juu ya mashina na matawi. Viko na umbo la duara dufu, rangi ya waridi na viko na poda ya laka nyeupe juu ya viwiliwili vyao. * Ishara za mimea kuathirika ni, ukuaji uliodumaa, kunyauka, matawi kubadili umbo, mashina kubadili rangi, kukunjamana kwa sehemu ya juu kabisa ya mimea na kufifia kwa mimea. * Sisimizi au chungu wanaweza pia kuwepo, kwa kuwa hulinda vidunguta ili waweze kula utomvu wanaoutoa vidunguta hao. * Kuvu iliyokama masizi meusi inaweza kukua kwenye matawi na mashina kwasababu ya utomvu uliopo. * Chukua hatua unapoona aina ya laka nyeupe kwenye ncha za miche, matawi na mashina; au wakati uonapo ishara zingine za kushambuliwa na vidunguta.

title: Kidungata cha muhogo
text: * Toa na uharibu mimea au sehemu za mimea zilizoathirika mwanzoni mwa kushambuliwa na vidunguta. * Pogoa mashina au matawi yaliyoathirika zaidi na uchome au uzike katika shimo lenye urefu wa zaidi ya sentimita 50. * Changanya gramu tano za sabuni (alata samina) pamoja na gramu tano za pilipili iliyopondwa, katika lita moja ya maji na uiache kwa nusu saa. Weka mchanganyiko huu katika shanta, halafu uongeze kiwango kifike hadi lita 15 za maji ndipo unyunyizie mimea. * Paka mafuta ya muarubaini, kwa mfano Grow-Safe. Tia mililita kumi za sabuni katika lita moja ya maji na ukoroge. Halafu ongeza mililita 50 za mafuta ya muarubaini, katika huo mchanganyiko wa maji na sabuni na uichanganye vizuri kabisa. Tia huu mchanganyiko wa mafuta-maji-sabuni katika lita 14 za maji yaliyo kwenye shanta,na uitumie ndani ya masaa manane. Zingatia kuwa imenyunyiziwa kwote. * Kama inawezekana tumia maadaui wao wa kawaida kama vile nyigu vimelea *Apoanagyrus lopezi* na wadudu-kibibi.

title: Kidungata cha muhogo
text: * Kama inawezekana tumia maadaui wao wa kawaida kama vile nyigu vimelea *Apoanagyrus lopezi* na wadudu-kibibi. * Dhibiti sisimizi au chungu, kwa kuwa wana uwezo wa kupunguza idadi ya maadui wa vidungata.

title: Fall armyworm on wheat.
text: CABI: Fall armyworm on wheat.

title: Fall armyworm on wheat.
text:
* Avoid late or off-season planting and avoid planting new crop near infested fields
* Avoid staggered planting (planting at different dates in the same field), as this provides a continous source of food for the pest
* Use short maturing and less preferred wheat varieties to escape the pest infestation that might occur later in the season
* Ensure optimum use of fertilizer for wheat plants to be able to compensate for damage done and apply at the right time
* Conserve shelters and flowering plants on the edges for beneficial insects such as ground beetles and parasitoids
* Destruction of volunteer wheat and weedy grasses in ditches around field margins can eliminate these sources of armyworms
* Rapid disposal of wheat residues after harvest

title: Fall armyworm on wheat.
text:
* After germination of seedlings, scout fields, at 5 or more spots, weekly (starting from the field margin) for larvae on plants and whether the problem is widespread or confined to certain areas or edges. * Caterpillars: light green to dark brown with longitudinal stripes. Dark head with an upside down pale Y-shaped marking on the front. The second-to-last body segment has four dark spots forming a square (3rd instar and above)
* Look for leaves that seem to have had all of their green tissue removed which gives the leaf a "window pane" appearance. Examine some plants showing evidence of injury, and look for small caterpillars. The suggested treatment threshold is 2-3 larvae per linear foot of row in wheat with active feeding symptoms. * Fall armyworm larvae feed primarily during the night and during cloudy weather. During the day, look for armyworms under loose soil and fallen leaves on the ground. * Use a pheromone with the Universal Bucket Trap to estimate adult moth population

title: Fall armyworm on wheat.
text:
* If available, spray young caterpillars with neem-based products before they move to neigbouring plants
* Use microbial biopesticides based on bacteria, fungi and viruses if available

title: Fall armyworm on rice.
text: CABI: Fall armyworm on rice.

title: Fall armyworm on rice.
text:
* Avoid late or off-season planting and dont plant new crop near infested fields
* Avoid staggered planting (planting at different dates in the same field), as this provides a continous source of food for the pest
* Use of fertilizers for rice plants to be vigorous and able to compensate for damage done and apply at the right time
* Use short maturing rice varieties that are less preferred by the fall armyworm to escape the pest infestation that might occur later in the season
* Establish your seedbeds far from large areas of weeds
* Reduce larval infestations by effective management of nearby grasses. Remove weeds from areas outside of fields and plough all fallow land
* Conserve shelters and flowering plants on the edges for beneficial insects such as predators and parasitoids
* Rapid disposal of rice residues after harvest

title: Fall armyworm on rice.
text:
* Sample plants every 10 feet along a line across the field and repeat this process in a second and third area, paying close attention to the crop margins
* Caterpillars: light green to dark brown with longitudinal stripes. Dark head with an upside down pale Y-shaped marking on the front. The second-to-last body segment has four dark spots forming a square (3rd instar and above)
* After germination of seedlings, scout fields weekly for larvae on plants and whether the problem is widespread or confined to certain areas or edges. * Fall armyworm are more likely to be a problem in late-planted fields and in fields surrounded by pasture. * Fall armyworm will feed initially on the foliage, then move to spikelets within the panicles, therefore they should also be monitored
* Use a pheromone with the Universal Bucket Trap to estimate adult moth population

title: Fall armyworm on rice.
text:
* On small-scale farms, hit or shake the foliage to make the fall armyworm larvae drop into the water and drown in paddy rice
* In paddy rice, flood infested fields for a few hours to kill the armyworm larvae. * Use microbial biopesticides based on bacteria, fungi and viruses if available

title: Fall armyworm on millet.
text: CABI: Fall armyworm on millet.

title: Fall armyworm on millet.
text:
* Avoid late planting to escape the pest attack. Plant immediately the onset of the rain, when the occurrence of the pest in the area is still low
* Deep plough the soil to expose insect stages hiding underground to birds and other natural enemies
* Use good quality seeds to increase plant vigour and potentially reduce damage
* Use millet varieties showing resistance/tolerance. Absence of foliage pubescence has been shown to reduce oviposition
* Use short maturing millet varieties to escape the pest outbreak that might occur later in the season
* Avoid staggered planting (planting at different dates in the same field), as this provides a continous source of food for the pest
* Ensure optimum use of fertilizer for strong millet plants able to withstand or compensate for pest damage and apply at the right time
* Intercropping with legumes helps to reduce pest pressure on both the millet and legume crops and supports natural enemies
* Conserve shelters and flowering plants on the edges for beneficial insects such as ground beetles and parasitoids

title: Fall armyworm on millet.
text:
* Monitor weekly for presence of the pest or symptoms such as fresh leaf damage or frass. Monitoring is important because you may reduce the cost of treating the whole field if you catch the larvae early
* Caterpillars: light green to dark brown with longitudinal stripes. Dark head with an upside down pale Y-shaped marking on the front. The second-to-last body segment has four dark spots forming a square (3rd instar and above)
* Caterpillars also feed during the night and completely defoliate the leaves, leaving only the midrib. Sometimes they also damage the earhead. * Egg mass: Cream/grey groups of 150-200 eggs covered in silk located on the underside or top of the leaves
* Millet is very tolerant of whorl stage defoliation. Treat when 50% whorls are infested and larvae are present. * Use a pheromone with the Universal Bucket Trap to estimate adult moth population

title: Fall armyworm on millet.
text:
* On small-scale farms, handpick and destroy the egg masses and larvae
* If available, spray young caterpillars with neem-based products before they enter the whorl
* Use microbial biopesticides based on bacteria, fungi and viruses if available

title: Aphids on chilli and green pepper.
text: CABI: Aphids on chilli and green pepper.

title: Aphids on chilli and green pepper.
text:
* *M. persicae*are small green aphids which feed on plant sap. These aphids can transmit plant viruses. * Use of repellant plants such as onion, garlic and marigold in alternate rows to crop. * Use of agro nets (size 400 µm) to prevent pest accessing crop seedlings, and remove at flowering stage
* Conserve natural enemies (e.g. ladybird beetles, hoverflies and parasitoid wasps) by avoiding use of broad spectrum insecticides and providing suitable habitat. * Avoid high levels of nitrogen in soil, as this causes plants to become succulent and attractive to aphids. * Remove and burn crop residues immediately after harvest.

title: Aphids on chilli and green pepper.
text:
* Start monitoring from seedling stage, look at lower leaves, stems or growing points for soft bodies insects, found in clusters. * Check underside of leaves, shoots and stems for immobile aphids. * Look for yellowing leaves, stunted growth and honeydew on infested crops. Sooty mould may grown on the honeydew. * Look for curled, wrinkled or cupped leaves and mosaic patterns on the leaves (alternating dark and light patches) - these are symptoms of viruses that can be transmitted by the aphid
* Monitor at least 3 times a week for aphids early in the morning/late in day during dry periods. * Start control measures when there is 10-20% infestation (i.e. 1-2 infested plants/10-20 plants in plots).

title: Aphids on chilli and green pepper.
text: * Remove and burn infested plants to help reduce population spread. * Use yellow traps (at 2 traps per 30 m2 to attract and kill aphids. * Spray soap solution (potassium soaps e.g. Alata samina). Add 10-15 tablespoons of liquid soal in 16 L knapsack and spray foliage. * Spray with neem-based products and follow label instructions (e.g. Azatrol, 1.2% Azadiractin. 1 part Azatrol with 1 part water, spray at 7-10 day intervals).

title: Aphids on eggplant.
text: CABI: Aphids on eggplant.

title: Aphids on eggplant.
text: * *M. persicae*are small aphids which feed on plant sap. These aphids can transmit plant viruses. * Cover plants with agro nets (400 µm mesh) to prevent pest access. * Grow aphid repellant plants (e.g. marigold and onions) as border/barrier of crop plots. * Burn dried cow dung and herb/shrub leaves to make smoke in early mornings or late evenings to prevent pest colonisation. * Apply poultry manure (850 kg/Ha) to ensure high plant vigour. * Conserve natural enemies by avoiding broad spectrum insecticides and providing suitable habitat.

title: Aphids on eggplant.
text:
* Begin monitoring at seedling stage, observe for associated ants around crops. * Observe underside of leaves for grey-black or green aphid insects (normally found in colonies). * Look for yellowing leaves, stunted growth and honeydew on infested crops. Sooty mould may grown on the honeydew. * Look for curled, wrinkled or cupped leaves and mosaic patterns on the leaves (alternating dark and light patches) - these are symptoms of viruses that can be transmitted by the aphid
* If 2-3 out of 20-30 plants have at least 2 aphid colonies, undertake control measures.

title: Aphids on eggplant.
text: * Wash infested areas of plants with a strong jet of water. * Use soapy water (1 ml/2 L water) on both sides of leaves, spray during early mornings/late evenings so spray does not dry quickly. * Release biocontrol agents (e.g. *Aphidius* spp., ladybirds, lacewings and parasitic wasps). Release roughly 5-25 per 100 square ft., weekly in areas of high infestation. * Spray with neem-based products and follow label instructions (e.g. Azatrol, 1.2% Azadiractin. 1 part Azatrol with 1 part water, spray at 7-10 day intervals).

title: Aphids on okro.
text: CABI: Aphids on okro.

title: Aphids on okro.
text: * *M. persicae*are small aphids which feed on plant sap. These aphids can transmit plant viruses. * Conserve natural enemies by avoiding use of broad spectrum insecticides and providing suitable habitat. * Use agro-nets (400 µm mesh) from seedling to vegetative stage to prevent aphid access. * Use aphid repellant plants (e.g. marigold, onion and/or garlic) in alternate rows amongst okro. * Use dry cow dung and green herb/shrub leaves to make smoke during early morning or late evening to repel aphids. * Apply poultry manure (after 1 week decomposition at 850 kg/Ha) to ensure high plant vigour.

title: Aphids on okro.
text:
* Begin monitoring seedling stage twice a week during early mornings and/or late evenings (especially during dry periods). * Observe for slow moving grey-black or green aphids, these are normally found in colonies on the underside of leaves as well as on new shoot tips and buds. * Observe for ants (linked with aphid presence) climbing up and down crop. * Look for yellowing leaves, stunted growth and honeydew on infested crops. Sooty mould may grown on the honeydew. * Look for curled, wrinkled or cupped leaves and mosaic patterns on the leaves (alternating dark and light patches) - these are symptoms of viruses that can be transmitted by the aphid
* At random, examine 20-30 plants, if 2-3 have at least 2 aphid colonies then undertake direct control measures.

title: Aphids on okro.
text: * Spray infested crops with a strong jet of water to remove aphids. * Use soap solution (potassium soap) (add 10-15 tablespoons of liquid soap and 1 L of water in a knapsack) to spray on plants. * Release biocontrol agents (e.g. *Aphidius* spp., ladybirds, lacewings and parasitic wasps). Release roughly 5-25 per 100 square ft., weekly in areas of high infestation. * Spray crops with botanical extracts (e.g. garlic, neem, red chilli pepper and soap). Take 50 g mixture of each in 2 L of water, boil for 15 minutes, cool then spray during evening.

title: Cassava root rot.
text: CABI: Cassava root rot.

title: Cassava root rot.
text:
* Cassava root rot is a disease caused by various types of fungi
* Select land that will not flood throughout the year and avoid water logged soil. * Avoid using planting materials from farms with reported cases of root rot diseases. * Select healthy plants for the production of planting materials, avoid plants that have wilted leaves. * Destroy plant debris (rotting stems, roots etc.) soon after harvest by burning or deep burying. * Avoid delaying the harvest of early maturing varieties. * Avoid continuous cropping on the same area of land/in infected zones, use crop rotations of at least 3 seasons with maize, millet or sorghum. * Clean farming tools after use with a 10% solution of household bleach. * Avoid planting cassava as first crop after clearance of woodland/forests to avoid fungal attacks.

title: Cassava root rot.
text: * Monitor fields regularly for develoment of yellow mushrooms in the soil or white fruiting bodies at base of crop stems - these fungi cause root rot. * Symptoms include wilting leaves, defoliation, stem dieback and death of infected plants. * In disease endemic areas, monitor farms for single or few wilted plants growing amongst healthy plants. * Storage roots of infected plants are swollen with soft brown rot internally. * Uproot any infected plant when identified and examine roots to establish cause of wilt. * Carry out control measures at the first sign of the disease.

title: Cassava root rot.
text: * Carefully remove fruiting bodies of the fungus and destroy immediately by burning. * Isolate plants with wilt symptoms and burn, take care for disrupting any fungus.

title: Whitefly on cassava.
text: CABI: Whitefly on cassava.

title: Whitefly on cassava.
text: * Whiteflies are small white insects that transmit viruses to the plants when feeding from the sap. * Clear weeds in advance of planting amongst crop to reduce overwintering pest stages. * Avoid use of broad spectrum insecticides to conserve natural enemies such as ladybirds, lacewings, hoverflies and parasitoids. Provide suitable habitat. * Remove and destroy ratoon cassava materials and other plant residues by burning or burying deep. * Plant repellent crops such as marigold around the boundary of the plot to repel whiteflies. * Provide suitable irrigation to crops, as stressed plants are more prone to whitefly damage. * Use resistant varieties against whitefly transmitted viruses (see information on Cassava mosaic virus and African cassava mosaic disease).

title: Whitefly on cassava.
text: * Monitor crops for whiteflies every week throughout the plant growth period (especially during the sprouting season). * For early detection, observe for white-brown eggs and white-yellow adults on the underside of leaves. * Look for a cloud of white insects which re-settle soon after disturbance of the plant. * Check for yellowing symptoms on the underside of leaves. * If 10-20 plants are observed with symptoms or at least 20 whiteflies on 10-20 plants/acre then follow direct control suggestions.

title: Whitefly on cassava.
text: * Use of yellow sticky traps to catch and kill adults (4 traps/300 m2 placed 50 cm above the ground). * Spray crops with Azadirachtin 0.03% (e.g. Nimbedicine EC, Nematech WG) 50 ml/20 L water 20 days after planting. * Release parasitic wasps such as *Encarsia formosa* if available in your area commercially. * Spray with entomopathogenic fungi such as *Verticillium lecanii*, *Beauveria bassiana*or *Paecilmyces fumosoroseus* if commercially available.

title: Webworm on cabbage.
text: CABI: Webworm on cabbage.

title: Webworm on cabbage.
text: * Widespread pest species, commonly found in food plants boring into stems and leaves. * Use of clean, pest-free seedlings from nurseries. * Remove plant material residues after harvest and destroy by burning or burying. * Till soil to remove cabbage stubbles and dispose of before planting new crops. * Practice crop rotation or intercropping with non-host plants (such as onion and carrot) to reduce webworm populations. * Use mustard or Chinese cabbage as trap crops in alternate rows. * Avoid use of broad spectrum insecticides to conserve natural enemies (spiders, parasistic wasps, lacewings and ants).

title: Webworm on cabbage.
text:
* Start monitoring after seedling emergence and check crops for larvae twice a week
* Inspect plants for egg masses, these are usually found in plant buds. Once eggs hatch the larvae feed on the underside of leaves and cover their bodies in webs. * A characteristic feature to observe is the larval webs covered in dirt and excrement. * The larva has a creamy white body with pale longitudinal stripes and a dark brown/black head, reaching 12-15 mm when fully grown. * Direct control measures should be followed once there are more than 1 larva per 5 plants.

title: Webworm on cabbage.
text:
* Hand pick and destroy caterpillars found on crops during lower infestation levels. * Plowing/removing weeds at least one month in advance prior to crop planting reduces potential webworm populations
* Use botanical extracts (such as neem seed extract, lemongrass or ginger) 1:15 L of water. * Use *Bacillus thurigiensis* and apply before larvae are protected by webs or in the centre of cabbages (which are difficult to reach by biopesticides). Apply once a week.

title: Aphids on tomato.
text: CABI: Aphids on tomato.

title: Aphids on tomato.
text: * Aphids are highly reproductive insects that can cause structural weakening of plants. * Avoid planting near aphid infested land or on land with a history of aphid infestation. * Active removal of weeds from plots to reduce aphid hosts. * Removal of alternative host species such as *Amaranthus*. Destroy by uprooting and burning or burying deep. * Intercropping with resistant species such as onion, garlic and parsley to reduce aphid populations. * Grow maize as a border around tomato field to attract flying aphids away from tomato crop.

title: Aphids on tomato.
text: * Monitoring should be undertaken soon after crop emergence until crop harvest. * Regularly check for leaf curling and sticky residue on crops at least once a week. * Observe underside of leaves for aphid presence. * High levels of aphid infestation may result in the presence of black sooty mould due to honeydew secretions from aphids. * When monitoring crops, sample the most recently expanded leaves (4th or 5th leaf from the growing point) to give an estimate action threshold. * If there is no presence of aphid-transmitted viruses in the area, small aphid populations are tolerable amongst crop. If infestation grows (5-10 plants per quarter acre of field) then undertake direct control measures.

title: Aphids on tomato.
text: * Prune leaves showing symptoms (curling, aphid populations on underside). * Removal and burning of infested crops to prevent spread of aphids to uninfested crops. * 10 tablespoons of liquid soap per 10 litres of water. Spray plants every week in the evening until aphid population has gone (this treatment is only effective during wet weather). Avoid overuse of soap sprays as this will burn the plant. * Spray neem oil products once a week for 4 weeks (4.5 ml/10 m2). Contact your local agro-input supplier to organise access of such products.

title: Aphids on rape.
text: CABI: Aphids on rape.

title: Aphids on rape.
text: * Aphids are highly reproductive, small insects that can weaken plant structures and transmit virus to crops. * Avoid planting near an infested crop or on land with a history of infestation. * Active removal of weeds from plots to reduce aphid hosts. * Removal of alternative host species such as *Amaranthus*. Destroy by uprooting and burning or burying deep. * Intercropping with pest repellent plants such as onion, garlic and parsley to reduce aphid populations close to rape. * Do not apply high levels of nitrogenous fertilizer as this will make the plants more attractive to aphids.

title: Aphids on rape.
text: * Regularly check for leaf curling on crop at leats once a week. * Observe underside of leaves for aphid presence. Aphids are small insects of 2 mm long, soft-bodied and green, brown or yellow in colour. * High levels of infestation may result in the presence of black sooty mould on leaves due to honeydew secretion from aphids. * Monitoring should be undertaken soon after crop emergence until crop harvest. * If there is no presence of aphid-transmitted viruses in the area, small aphid populations are tolerable amongst crop. * If infestation grows (10-20% por 1-2 infested plants per 10-20 observed) then consider undertaking direct control measures.

title: Aphids on rape.
text: * Prune leaves showing symptoms (curling, aphid populations on underside). * Removal and burning of infested crops to prevent spread of the fungus. * Spray neem oil products once a week for 4 weeks (4.5 ml/10 m2). Contact your local agro-input supplier to organise access of such products. * Use of soap water solution spray on crops to wash off any aphids present (1 tablespoons of liquid soap per 10 litres of water)

title: Red spider mite on jasmine-India.
text: Red spider mite on jasmine-India.

title: Red spider mite on jasmine-India.
text:
* Provide intermittent irrigation – preferably once a week during the summer months (March to June)
* Removal of alternate host & weeds like – *Tridaz procumbens* (Tamil Name: கிணற்றடிப்பூண்டு). * Grow resistant varieties of Jasmine, i.e. Co-4. * Removal of infested plants from the field.

title: Red spider mite on jasmine-India.
text: * Observe in the evening during vegetative stages for yellowing & reddish leaves caused by mites sucking sap from the lower surface of the leaves. This should be done on a weekly basis. * Also look for drying, withering and the formation of silken webs on the plant. * Observe for reddish mites on leaves with a hand lens.

title: Red spider mite on jasmine-India.
text:
* Apply Pungam Oil
* (*Pongamia glabra*) at 2ml / litre of water along with 100 gm of kadhi soap over foliage. 4 sprays at 15 day intervals. * Spray bioacaricide – *Hirsutella thompsonii* at 4 gm/lit of water during dawn hours.

title: Red spider mite on jasmine-India.
text: * When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval. Do not empty into drains and water sources.

title: Red spider mite on jasmine-India.
text:
### Spray Wettable Sulphur 50 WP at 2 gm/l of water ###
Sulphur falls under WHO Class III (slightly hazardous). ### If the infestation is severe, spray Propargite 57% EC at 2 ml/l of water. ###
Propargite falls under WHO Class III (slightly Hazardous).

title: Red-banded thrips on cashew.
text: UK, CABI: Red-banded thrips on cashew.

title: Red-banded thrips on cashew.
text: * Thrips are tiny insects that cause damage to crop plants by feeding on the surface of the leaves and fruits. * Establish windbreaks before orchard planting. * Maintain good cultural practices to increase plant vigour and enhance plant tolerance to thrip damage (sufficient fertilizer application, pruning, plant spacing etc.). * Keep the soil well irrigated, avoid excessive application of nitrogen fertilizers which may promote thrip populations. * Conserve natural enemies of *S. rubrocinctus* such as spiders, predatory mites, lacewings and predatory bugs (e.g. minute pirate bug) by avoiding the use of broad spectrum insecticides. * Prune trees to allow lighter conditions within the orchard (unfavourable conditions for thrips).

title: Red-banded thrips on cashew.
text: * Plant parts attacked first show chlorotic spots and later turn to a silvery coloration. * Weekly, shake foliage/flowers over a white tray and observe for presence of nymphs with red bands on abdomen and black, elongated bodied adults. * Take note of clustered fruit, as low infestation levels show thrip preference to feed between clustered fruit rather than single fruit. * Sticky blue traps can be used to monitor the presence of thrips. * Observe plants for sooty mould, a symptom of thrip infestation. * Population numbers are higher during the dry season and severe attacks can result in premature leaf drop, the inflorescences drying and the pseudofruit can even crack. * Take direct control actions before silvery leaves turn brown/appear burnt or when 4-6 adults are found per flower.

title: Red-banded thrips on cashew.
text: * Use pheromone lures in mass trappings, add a contaminant to kill trapped thrips. * Use of neem based products e.g. neem seed oil extract and Buprofezin or neem oil soap spray (check product label for dosage or 3 tablespoons of liquid soap per litre of water). * Use of biological pesticides e.g. *Metarhizum anisopliae* or *Beauveria bassiana* and follow instructions and dosage on the labels.

title: Longtailed mealybug on cashew.
text: UK, CABI: Longtailed mealybug on cashew.

title: Longtailed mealybug on cashew.
text: * Use planting materials with certified planting material to reduce spread of infestation into new fields. * Avoid the use of broad spectrum pesticides to encourage natural enemies (lacewings, pirate bugs, lady beetles) and parasitoids (*Tetracnemoidea sydneyensis* or *T.peregrina*). * Collect any fallen leaves and plant material below cashew trees and destroy by burning to prevent the spread of mealybug pests.

title: Longtailed mealybug on cashew.
text: * Observe for small, oval shaped insects with long tails (roughly a quarter of their body length) and a defined stripe running down the back. * Look for mealybugs between clusters of berries, on soft stems, flower buds, twigs, near the main root where soil is loose and the upper side of leaves. * Symptoms of mealybug infestations include delayed ripening, abnormal shapes and premature dropping of fruit. Sooty mould on leaf surfaces which can cause leaves to turn yellow and drop. * Use of yellow sticky traps with a pheromone lure to monitor for adults, follow product label for guidance. * Inspect plants anytime of day, monitor more frequently during dry periods. * As soon as mealybugs are identified in your fields, undertake direct control actions. * Consider direct control actions as soon as symptoms are observed.

title: Longtailed mealybug on cashew.
text: * Use a strong jet of water to dislodge insects from plants. * Burn or bury (50 cm deep) any infested plant parts. * Prune highly infested plant areas such as stems or leaves and then destroy. * Control ant populations as they reduce natural predator populations. * Use of soap spray (one bar of soap in 20 L of water) to remove insect infestation from plants. * Apply 1-2% vegetable oil (e.g. neem oil) as a spray on plants (10 ml of liquid soap to 1 litre of water, add 50 ml of neem oil). * Paste a grease band (5 cm wide) on the main stem of the plant to prevent pests from crawling up to the leaves and fruit.

title: Larger grain borer on cassava.
text: UK, CABI: Larger grain borer on cassava.

title: Larger grain borer on cassava.
text: * If pest is known to be found in your area, then remove all plant residue from previous harvest and burn. * Use clean and well ventilated storage facilities. * Leave cassava roots in the ground for as long as possible to reduce storage period and losses due to pest. * After harvesting cassava, sun dry the crop and transfer to sealed containers immediately. * Use suitable containers for storing crops (appropriately sealed to prevent access from pests), the insect can easily attack crop stored in bags.

title: Larger grain borer on cassava.
text: * Monitor stored cassava weekly for damage (e.g. entry/exit holes from insect) and adults or larva. Infestation at low levels is not obvious, so monitoring should be done carefully. * Look for small beetles (3 - 4.5 mm) with a uniform dark brown-black body. * Look for exit holes in cassava and dust on the ground. * Install male-released aggregation pheromone traps in susceptible areas to monitor pest populations (at least 100 m away from crop/storage areas). Check traps regularly and replace the lure following the product label instructions. * Note: Pheromone traps will not work within storage areas as *P. truncatus* will not respond when on its food. * Consider direct control actions as soon as grain borers are identified.

title: Larger grain borer on cassava.
text: * Use of biocontrol agent such as the predatory beetle *Teretrius nigrescens*. Contact your local government office to inquire about release in your area. * Use metal silos or similar storage options for crop, rather than bags and other easily-accessible materials for the insect to infest.

title: Bean seed fly.
text: UK, CABI: Bean seed fly.

title: Bean seed fly.
text: * Bean seed fly is a pest that feed on the swollen, ungerminated seed of vegetable crops at larval stage, called maggot. * The use of winter cover crops (e.g. grasses) may increase fly populations, if this is needed then plant bean crop 3.5 weeks after the cover crop has been incorportated into the soil. * Avoid planting during wet periods to reduce infestation of maggots. Plant crops when the weather and soil promotes rapid germination to reduce impact of maggots. * Remove flowering weeds from the area to reduce nearby food sources for flies.

title: Bean seed fly.
text: * When monitoring fields, look out for wilting plants and gaps in vegetation where seedlings have failed to emerge. To identify maggots, search in the soil around these areas. * Maggots can also be found tunneling up the stem of newly emerged seedlings. * Eggs: 1-2 mm long, white eggs. * Larvae: Up to 10 mm long, white maggots. Pupae are brown and are up to 7 mm long. * Adults: Small, grey bodied flies, up to 5.2 mm long. * The symptoms can be confused with wireworm feeding injury and dieback

title: Bean seed fly.
text: * The only method for controlling *D. platura* is targeting the maggot stage. Seed treatments are the cheapest and most effective control for maggots.

title: Bakanae disease of paddy-India.
text: Bakanae disease of paddy-India.

title: Bakanae disease of paddy-India.
text: * Seed transmission is very common. Clean and healthy seeds should be used to minimize disease occurrence. * Use 10% salt water to separate lightweight and infected seeds. Wash the grains after sorting to remove the salt. * Apply recommended level of Nitrogenous fertilizer in three split doses: 50% basal, 25% in tillering and 25% in panicle initiation stage. Avoid excess application of Nitrogen fertilizer. * Store grains with 13.5-14% moisture content.

title: Bakanae disease of paddy-India.
text: * Visit the nursery and main field at weekly intervals. * Be vigilant especially during the periods of high temperature and high humidity at flowering as this favours disease spread. * Look for plants with abnormally tall seedlings with pale, thin leaves, and fewer tillers. * Look for white growth of the pathogen at the base or on the lower sheath of the infected plant. * Look for adventitious roots growing from above-ground nodes on the stem. * Look for unhealthy seedlings drying from the bottom to top at early tillering stage, which eventually die after few days.

title: Bakanae disease of paddy-India.
text: * Carefully rogue out (so as not to spread) and destroy (burn or bury) infected or dead plants, both from nursery and main field as soon as identified. * Seed treatment with *Trichoderma asperellum* @ 5 g/kg seed.

title: Bakanae disease of paddy-India.
text: * Use personal protective equipment (PPEs) such as gloves, mask and goggles.

title: Bakanae disease of paddy-India.
text:
### Before transplanting, dip the seedling in 0.2 % solution (2 ml in one lit) of Azoxystrobin 23% SC for 6 hours. ###
WHO class U (unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use). FRAC code 11. ### Spray Azoxystrobin 23% SC 250ml/acre ###
WHO class U (unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use). FRAC code 11. ### Spray Tebuconazole + Trifloxystrobin (25% +50% mix) at 80g/acre on appearance of disease symptoms ###
WHO class ll (moderately hazardous). FRAC codes 3 and 11 respectively. ### Spray Propiconazole 25 EC at 0.1% (1 ml/L water) at boot stage for seed crop. ###
WHO class ll (moderately hazardous). FRAC code 3.

title: Brinjal fruit and shoot borer-India.
text: Brinjal fruit and shoot borer-India.

title: Brinjal fruit and shoot borer-India.
text: * Deep Summer Ploughing in May-June. * Early plant seedlings to avoid pest attack (Adjust time of Planting to late Feb/early March). * Use less susceptible varieties viz., PPL, PPC, Punjab Neelam and Punjab Barsati. * Sowing of coriander on ridges will encourage natural enemies. * Follow crop rotation using okra, tomato, cucubits, cruciferous vegetables or summer pulses. * Avoid Monocropping if possible. * Avoid the use of broad spectrum insecticides to promote natural enemies (such as predatory ants, ladybirg beetles, praying mantis and spiders).

title: Brinjal fruit and shoot borer-India.
text: * Regularly monitor the crop to observe holes on leaf petioles, growing points of shoots or on fruits; as well as drying-up of terminal shoots. * Other symptoms of infestation include wilting of leaves, yield loss, weakened plant stems and poor fruit development. * Larvae can grow up to 155 mm long and are reddish coloured. Adults have a wingspan of 18-24 mm and have characteristic white wing patterns with a brown patch and black spots. * Use pheromone traps to observe the presence of moths; use 1-2 traps per acre placed above plant canopy. Action threshold is 3 moths per trap.

title: Brinjal fruit and shoot borer-India.
text: * Clip and destroy infested shoots and fruits along with larvae twice a week; buried deep in the soil. * Apply neem cake at a rate of 100 kg/acre after 30 days of transplanting. * Installation of pheromone traps 4-6 traps/acre for mass trapping of male moths. Change the lure after 15 days. * Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma chilonis or Trichogramma pretiosum at 10 days intervals of 50000-60000 per acre, once trap catch threshold reached. * Spray neem based insecticides viz., NSKE 5% or Neem oil at 3 ml/litre of water. * Spray B.t.var. kurstaki at 1-1.5 kg/Ha (e.g. Dipel).

title: Brinjal fruit and shoot borer-India.
text: * Use Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) while using Insecticides. * Follow pesticide rotation to avoid pest resistance.

title: Brinjal fruit and shoot borer-India.
text:
### Dipping of seedling in Imidacloprid for 3-4 hours at a rate of 1 ml per litre of water before transplanting. ###
WHO class II (Moderately hazardous)
### Flubendamide 48SC or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% at 0.5 ml/litre of water; or Emamectin benzoate 5% SG at a rate of 1 gm/ litre of water; or cartap hydrochloride 50%SP 3 gm/litre of water. ###
WHO class II (Moderately Hazardous) apart from Chlorantraniliprole WHO Class -U (Unlikely to present acute hazards in normal use)

title: Fruit and shoot borer of okra-India.
text: Fruit and shoot borer of okra-India.

title: Fruit and shoot borer of okra-India.
text:
* Remove and destroy affected fruits and shoots; for shoots by
nipping them off below pest hole. * Grow carrot, sunflower and buckwheat to attract pest away from okra. * Cover beds with polythene sheet 45 gauge (0.45 mm) thickness for three weeks before sowing, this will reduce the pest in the soil. * Use pheromone traps (5-8 per acre), put at least one foot above the crop canopy. * Avoid growing Malvaceous crops (cotton, hollyhock ) in sequence. * Deep plough fields during summer.

title: Fruit and shoot borer of okra-India.
text: * Look for withered and drooping terminal shoots, shedding of buds and flowers, bore holes in fruits and deformed fruits. * Look for blue eggs on the underside of leaves and brown, boat shaped larvae in terminal shoots and fruits. * Set up pheromone traps (3-5 per acre). If 2-4 silvery green adults are caught per trap then consider direct control actions.

title: Fruit and shoot borer of okra-India.
text:
* Release egg parasitoid *Trichogramma chilonis* at a rate of 40,000 per acre. * Apply neem cake at 100 kg/acre at the time of transplanting. * Spray azadirachtin 0.03% (300 ppm) as neem oil at a rate of 1000-2000 ml in 200-400 litres of water per acre. * Apply azadirachtin 5% w/w neem extract concentrate at 80 ml in 160 litres of water per acre
* Conserve predators of the borer, such as coccinellids, parasitic wasps, dragonflies, spiders, robber flies, reduviid bugs, praying mantis, fire ants, earwings and ground beetles.

title: Fruit and shoot borer of okra-India.
text:
* Use personnel protection equipments (PPE)
while using chemical pesticides

title: Fruit and shoot borer of okra-India.
text:
### Spray crop with chloranthraniliprole 18.5% SC (50 ml in 200 L of water/acre). ###
WHO class U (unlikely to present acute hazard). ### Cypermethrin 25% EC (60-80 ml in 200 L of water/acre). ###
WHO class II (moderately hazardous). ### Deltamethrin 2.8% EC (160-240 ml in 160-240 L of water/acre). ###
WHO class II (moderately hazardous). ### During flowering stage spray with Spinosad (2 ml/litre of water). ###
WHO class III (slightly hazardous).

title: Sheath blight of rice-India.
text: Sheath blight of rice-India.

title: Sheath blight of rice-India.
text: * Good field sanitation before and during season, including clearing plant debris from the previous harvest. * Deep summer ploughing to expose disease to sun; good drainage. * Use tolerant varieties: 1121, Pusa Basmati 1509. * Fertilize based on soil health card. * Soil application of *Pseudomonas fluorescens* (2.5 kg/ha with 100 kg of FYM at field preparation). * Treat seed with Carbendazim at a rate of 2 g/kg of seed (see restrictions). * Avoid close planting. * Sow short duration varieties such as IET-1410, RATNA, PC-19.

title: Sheath blight of rice-India.
text: * Check for brownish, irregular semi circles on sheath, stem and leaves. * Check for whitish cottony growth (mycelium) on leaf sheath/blade near the water line. * Check for minute ball like structure (sclerotia) on leaf sheath near the water line. * Be extra vigilent 30 to 35 days after transplanting and onward. * If around 5% of plants show symptoms use then consider direct control actions.

title: Sheath blight of rice-India.
text: * Foliar application of *Pseudomonas fluorescens* at a rate of 2.5 kg/Ha with 500 L of water when threshold reached. * Drain off standing water from the infected field.

title: Sheath blight of rice-India.
text: * Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) is recommended while using chemical pesticides.

title: Sheath blight of rice-India.
text:
### Spray with Carbendazim at a rate of 0.1% at appearance of disease or 250-300 gm/acre with 150 litres of water. ###
WHO U (unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use). Foliar application. Maximum of two applications with 15 day interval. Use at maximum tillering stage. Be careful as can kill important pollinators such as honeybees.

title: Stripe rust of wheat-India.
text: Stripe rust of wheat-India.

title: Stripe rust of wheat-India.
text: * Sow resistant varieties for irrigated/unirrigated areas. * Timely sowing (first week of November). * Seed treatment with tebucinazole (2 g/kg of seed). * Apply balanced dose of NPK. * Promote cultivation of resistant varieties for fodder purpose. * Seed replacement every 3-4 years. * Sowing of mosaic of 2-3 varieties at village level. * Avoid promotion of cultivation of a single variety on larger areas. * Strictly follow irrigation schedule. * Cleaning of clothes and shoes after visiting infected field.

title: Stripe rust of wheat-India.
text: * Look for yellow stripes/turmeric powder (spores) on flag leaves (upper most); if there is no powder it may be spot blotch or a nutritional deficiency. * Undertake strict monitoring in water logged areas. * Monitoring after 60 days (last week of December) in irrigated areas and after 30 days in late sown areas of wheat. * Be more vigilant when dew formation takes place. * Share monitoring information at community level, village level, district level and state level. * Check crops three times a week from January onwards.

title: Stripe rust of wheat-India.
text:
### Foliar application of propiconazole or tebuconazole at a rate of 1 ml/L of water on the appearance of symptom(s). ###
WHO class II (moderately hazardous). ### Crop raised for seed purpose, apply foliar application of Propiconazole or Tebuconazole (1 ml/L of water during first week of February). ###
WHO class II (moderately hazardous). Apply at tillering stage and repeat spray after 15-day interval. However avoid spraying during rains. ### Tilt/Folicur (Trizoles), Systemic/ FRAC. ###
May harm aquatic organisms.

title: Tomato fruit borer-India.
text: Tomato fruit borer-India.

title: Tomato fruit borer-India.
text: * Deep summer ploughing. * Early planting can help avoid this pest. * Avoid monocropping. Grow simultaneously 40 day-old African marigold with 25 day-old tomato seedling, in the 1:16 rows. * Correctly space your seeds/seedlings. Spacing depends upon variety but in general should be 60x 45 cm. * Install bird perches in the field to encourage predatory birds. * Avoid the use of broad spectrum insecticides to conserve natural pest enemies (such as spiders, ants, parasitic wasps and robberflies).

title: Tomato fruit borer-India.
text: * Regular monitoring of the crop to check for caterpillars on the leaves, ideally during morning and evening hours.Threshold is 5-10% of leaves infested. * Use pheromone and/or light traps to check for the presence of the adult moths. Use 1 trap per acre. Action threshold is 3 or more adult moths in a trap.

title: Tomato fruit borer-India.
text: * Install pheromone traps (5 traps per acre) for mass trapping of male moths. Change the lure every 15 days. * Install light traps to attract and kill adult moths. * Release the egg parasitoid *Trichogramma brassilences* or *T. pretiosum* at a rate of 40000-60000 parasitoids per acre once the action threshold is reached, or at the time of flowering. Repeat at 15-day intervals. * Spray neem-based insecticides e.g. NSKE (5%or Neem oil at a rate of 3 ml/L of water). * Foliar spray of the virus HaNPV (250 LE/Ha) with 20 Jaggery in the evening hours. * Foliar spray of the bacterium *Bacillus thuringiensis* var. kurstaki (1-1.5 kg/Ha). * Spray *Beauveria bassiana* following instructions and dosage on the labels.

title: Tomato fruit borer-India.
text: * Follow pesticide rotation to avoid pest resistance. * Frequency of spray depends upon the pest intensity. * Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) isrecommended while using chemical pesticides.

title: Tomato fruit borer-India.
text:
### Spray the crop with Spinosad 45 SC at a rate of 0.5 ml/L. ###
WHO Class III (slightly hazardous). ### Spray with either of the following: Flubendamide 48 SC, Chlorantraniliprole 18.5%, Indoxacarb at 0.1% or HaNPV at 250LE and a half dose of any of the aforementioned chemicals. ###
Flubendamide and Indoxacarb WHO Class II (moderately hazardous); Chlorantraniliprole WHO Class U (unlikely to present acute hazards in normal use). ### Spray with Cyantraniliprole 10.26% OD following instructions and dosage on the labels. ###
WHO Class U (unlikely to present acute hazards in normal use). PHI 3 days. ### Spray with Fluxametamide 10% EC following instructions and dosage on the labels. ###
Spray with Fluxametamide 10% EC following instructions and dosage on the labels.

title: Aphids on beans.
text: CABI: Aphids on beans.

title: Aphids on beans.
